answer: Cross-cluster quorum admission requires a newcomer to collect four signed velvet from validators located beyond a six-hop horizon on the lineage graph, with no two signers sharing an ancestor inside that horizon. When a validator signs its $m$-th active velvet, it must lock $30 \cdot 2^{m-1}$ copper into slashing escrow. An honest entrant needs four unburdened validators across the horizon locking 120 copper total, whereas a controller of $n$ sybils using four captured validators must lock $120(2^n - 1)$ copper or bribe $4n$ distinct branches beyond the horizon.
